agent_authored.description: Brian2 is a widely used simulator for spiking neural networks in which models are written as plain-text differential equations; it generates and compiles simulation code at runtime (numpy, Cython) or ahead of time (C++ standalone device). Pinned at release 2.10.1, commit 3fe5ac9a9898210319a159160fd880d5a4a21205. Citation: Stimberg, Brette, Goodman, eLife 8:e47314 (2019), doi 10.7554/eLife.47314.

agent_authored.generated_vendor_third_party_notes: No vendored third-party code trees. 21 of 23 .pyx files are runtime templates compiled into a per-user on-disk cache at simulation time; only synapses/cythonspikequeue.pyx and memory/cythondynamicarray.pyx are built at install time. C++ codegen templates live under brian2/devices/cpp_standalone/templates/ as jinja2 files.

breakdown.rule: approximate: a text file is third-party when under measurement.third_party_paths, else a test when under a test path marker or named test_*, else an example when under an example path marker, else production when its extension is in measurement.source_extensions, else other

approval.human_ref: single-module default: the whole codebase is one module; no human decision at STOP 1, the cut is read in the source PR body at STOP 2

cp -r brian2-2.10.1 brian2-build  # scratch copy, pristine checkout untouched

modules.title: Brian2 spiking neural network simulator (whole codebase, single module)
entrypoints: python -c 'import brian2' (the package is the product; models are Python scripts using NeuronGroup/Synapses/Network)
brian2.test() (official test driver, brian2/tests/__init__.py:run, repeats the pytest suite per codegen target)
modules.expensive_path: simulation time loops: per-timestep state updates, threshold/reset and synaptic propagation over the network; cost scales with neurons x synapses x timesteps, plus one-off Cython/C++ compilation of every generated code object
modules.rationale: one Python package with one official test suite and one driver; the four codegen targets are configurations of the same objects, not separable components, and the official tests parametrize over targets via pytest markers
excluded: docs_sphinx/ and tutorials/ (documentation, no simulation code)
dev/ (maintainer tools, incl. run_examples.py docs harness)
brian2/sphinxext/ (Sphinx extensions, not exercised by simulation tests)
hazards: RNG streams differ between runtime device and cpp_standalone device: same seed does not reproduce across targets (RuntimeDevice.seed -> np.random.seed vs seed queued into generated C++ main)
Synapses.connect(p=...) draws rand() in generated code: stochastic unless seeded
cython runtime target compiles into an on-disk per-user cache (filelock): first runs pay compile time, cache dir must be writable
test_neurongroup.py::test_namespace_warnings is order-dependent: fails in a full-file run, passes alone (warning bookkeeping leaks between tests)
brian2/tests/test_network.py contains very slow or hanging entries in this environment (full file exceeded 9 min; under per-test diagnosis)
modules.purpose: one Python package with one official test suite and one driver; the four codegen targets are configurations of the same objects, not separable components, and the official tests parametrize over targets via pytest markers
primary_inputs: model equations as Python strings (Equations objects)
NeuronGroup/Synapses/PoissonGroup construction parameters and initial values
preferences (prefs.codegen.target and friends) and device selection (set_device)
primary_outputs: recorded state variables and spike trains via StateMonitor/SpikeMonitor/PopulationRateMonitor
final state variable arrays on groups
generated+compiled code artifacts (Cython cache dir, cpp_standalone project dir)
algorithm_stages: parse equations and check units (brian2/equations/, brian2/units/)
build abstract code and apply numerical integration method (brian2/stateupdaters/)
generate target code from templates and compile it (brian2/codegen/, brian2/devices/)
run the clock-driven loop: state update, threshold, spike propagation via spike queue, reset, monitors (brian2/core/network.py, brian2/synapses/)
unique_responsibilities: the entire simulation pipeline from equation strings to numbers
codegen for all four targets and their runtime caches
not_responsible_for: docs_sphinx/ and tutorials/ (documentation, no simulation code)
dev/ (maintainer tools, incl. run_examples.py docs harness)
brian2/sphinxext/ (Sphinx extensions, not exercised by simulation tests)
modules.differences: single-module codebase; no sibling modules to differ from
evidence: brian2/tests/__init__.py:run() drives one suite over all targets
brian2/conftest.py resets prefs/defaultclock/device per test for every target
